title: Derived Hom and object descent for a normalized native functor
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $X$ a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible in every local ring. Let $D$ be a normalized native functor of [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-normalized-functor]. For every two source objects $K,L$, its map from $\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)$ to the full ambient derived $\operatorname{Hom}(D.JK,D.JL)$ is bijective. For every native derived object $M$, bounded adic constructibility in the sense of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework] holds if and only if $M$ is isomorphic to $D.JA$ for some source object $A$. This proves properties of the given functor and does not construct its coefficient maps or comparisons.

source.place: Native realization proof step 3 (constructibility comparison) and steps 6--7 (Hom and object descent).

proof.text: These ring identifications give equivalences of their module categories, preserving underlying sheaves, kernels and cokernels. The convention of $\mathcal A_T$ takes $B_T$-module objects in sheaves of $\underline\Omega$-modules under $\otimes_{\underline\Omega}$. Locally constant functions lie in $B_T$, so $\underline\Omega\to B_T$ is a ring map; the unit axiom makes the given $\underline\Omega$-structure the restricted one, and every $B_T$-action factors through the epimorphism $B_T\otimes M\to B_T\otimes_{\underline\Omega}M$. So these are the $B_T$-module objects in abelian sheaves. Internal modules and sectionwise module sheaves agree by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]; transport along a coefficient isomorphism has the explicit inverse and tensor normalization of [lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso]. The induced exact equivalences act termwise on complexes and descend with their shifts and triangles by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Under them the condensed bounded constructible category $\mathcal C_T^c(\Omega)$ equals $\mathcal C_T$: local finite presentation implies local finite freeness by [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-lfp-local-triviality], and a finite free module is the cokernel of $0\to A^r$. The finite-$E$ version follows from [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-lfp-local-triviality]. These assertions apply on each Noetherian stratum. The local-on-$T$ stratifications defining $\mathcal C_T$ can be made finite globally: choose a finite open subcover $U_1,\ldots,U_m$ and partition $T$ into the locally closed pieces $U_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}U_j$. Pull each given stratification on $U_i$ to this piece by fiber products. These finitely many locally closed scheme strata cover $T$ disjointly and the local finite-free models restrict to them. Thus neither boundedness nor a global stratification condition changes in this comparison.

proof.text: For an already given normalized functor D, its integral natural comparison determines its finite-stage restriction, after raw rationalization, as the usual finite-field realization followed by native extension. Its common-field equation makes the maps between these restrictions agree with the finite-stage completion and balanced scalar comparisons. Thus all Hom colimit transition maps used below coincide with D.J.map.

Let $(E,K)$ and $(F,L)$ be two source objects. At every common finite $H\supseteq E,F$, full faithfulness of $R_{T,H}$ identifies the Hom group between their $H$-extensions with the corresponding derived Hom group in $\mathcal C_T^c(H)$. Step 5 identifies the transition maps in these systems. Taking their filtered colimit therefore identifies the source Hom set with the common-field Hom colimit for the condensed categories. By [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit], this last colimit maps bijectively to the ambient derived Hom between their $B_T$-realizations. This is exactly the map induced by $J_T$, so $J_T$ is full and faithful. Replacing $L$ by $L[r]$ gives the same conclusion in every integer degree, not merely in the heart.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2): full faithfulness; the existing condensed two-colimit supplies derived object/Hom descent

proof.text: Given $M\in\mathcal C_T$, view it as an object of $\mathcal C_T^c(\Omega)$ using steps 2–3. By [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit], choose a finite $E$ and $M_E\in\mathcal C_T^c(E)$ with $B_T\otimes^L_{E_T}M_E\cong M$. By essential surjectivity of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], choose $K_E\in D^b_c(T,E)$ with $R_{T,E}K_E\cong M_E$. Tensor transitivity of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus] now gives $J_T(E,K_E)\cong M$. Hence $J_T$ is essentially surjective and, with step 6, an equivalence. Every source distinguished triangle is represented at one finite field by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Its image is distinguished because $R_{T,E}$ and further derived scalar extension are triangulated by the cited statements. Conversely every morphism between target objects comes from a source morphism; its source cone realizes to an ambient cone. Thus $\mathcal C_T$ has the inherited triangulated structure and $J_T$ is the asserted triangulated equivalence.
